description: Models the hydrogen bond as the h²-suppressed weak crossing of the substrate q-deformation parameter h = q₀−q₀⁻¹ ≈ 0.209: E_HB = h²·E_cov, h² ≈ 0.0437 ≈ the measured H-bond/covalent ratio (~0.044). Per-molecule cohesion L = n_HB·h²·E_cov with net H-bond count from the braid/VSEPR. No fit (h² from q₀; E_cov and L_obs experimental inputs; n_HB from lone-pair structure). RESULT: period-2 hydrogen-bonders H₂O and HF land within ~1–2% of measured latent heat; period-3+ hydrides (H₂S/Se/Te) are over-predicted by the unsuppressed form (they do not H-bond; L is dispersion-dominated), flagging the period-n lone-pair suppression as the next open piece. Wires prop:quantum-ideal-gas-law (T_q=ℏ_q) + the boltzmann-constant Kelvin bridge k_B T_phys = ℏ_q.

data.finding: The hydrogen bond is the h²-suppressed weak crossing of the substrate q-deformation parameter h = q₀−q₀⁻¹: E_HB = h²·E_cov, h² ≈ 0.0437 ≈ the measured H-bond/covalent ratio. With net H-bond counts from the braid/VSEPR, the no-fit cohesion L = n_HB·h²·E_cov reproduces the latent heat of the period-2 hydrogen-bonders H₂O (~1%) and HF (~2%). Period-3+ hydrides are over-predicted because they do not actually H-bond (their L is dispersion-dominated); capturing that needs the period-n lone-pair suppression (the same (n) structure as the H₂S 1/√5/(n-1)² result). T_boil then follows from L/ΔS_vap, with ΔS_vap the next q-entropy quantity (⟨S_q⟩ / ice-residual). Tier: near-match (O,F); open (period-n).
